doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Milt Hinton tribute at the 92nd Street Y and goodbye
summary: He will play Hinton's part in 'The Judge and the Jury' at the 92nd Street Y, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: I will say though that I am very grateful for the opportunity that I have coming up in July, at the 92nd Street Y, you know those concerts every July for a week or two. Dick Hyman is the musical director of the concert series at the 92nd Street Y in Manhattan, and he’s doing a tribute to Milt this year on one of the nights. And he’s going to have a piece written by Milt called “The Judge and the Jury.” I’ve heard it by two titles: “The Judge Meets the Section,” and “The Judge Meets the Jury.” And on that Columbia release, “Laughing at Life,” it’s called “The Judge and the Jury.” And we’re going to do that piece and I’m going to get the Milt Hinton part.
Yeah. Because of the slapping involved.
Which I heard you do the other night.
Yeah. And he listed, did he say Jay Leonhart and Jack Lesberg and Ron Carter and Rufus Reid are going to be the other bass players. So that’s going to be a great honor.
Now I’ve got to run home and learn the piece. I hope you have good editing capabilities.
Well thanks for your time. I appreciate it.
All right. Thanks, Monk. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -24-
